key_concept: Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) spread mainly through sexual contact; tuberculosis is an airborne bacterial infection and is not an STI.
steps: Syphilis is caused by the bacterium $Treponema\ pallidum$ and spreads through sexual contact. It is an STI.
Gonorrhoea is caused by the bacterium $Neisseria\ gonorrhoeae$ and spreads through sexual contact. It is an STI.
Genital warts are caused by Human Papilloma Virus (HPV) and spread through sexual contact. They are an STI.
Tuberculosis is caused by $Mycobacterium\ tuberculosis$. It spreads mainly through air, via droplets released when an infected person coughs or sneezes, and is not transmitted sexually.
So the disease that is not sexually transmitted is tuberculosis.
why_not_others: Syphilis, gonorrhoea and genital warts are all part of the standard STI list (along with genital herpes, chlamydiasis, trichomoniasis, hepatitis B and HIV/AIDS), so none of them can be the answer.
common_trap: Students may wrongly link TB with HIV/AIDS because TB is a common opportunistic infection in AIDS patients, and then assume TB is also sexually transmitted.
time_saving_tip: Memorise the standard STI list: gonorrhoea, syphilis, genital herpes, chlamydiasis, genital warts, trichomoniasis, hepatitis B and HIV/AIDS. Any option outside this list is the answer.
